mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as stronger labor market momentum supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month AND HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: In periods satisfying the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to coincide with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA of INDPRO for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive or are significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly spikes above 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days tends to be negative due to market anticipation of tighter monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 AND lag(CPIAUCSL) <= 2.9 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain non-negative or are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during the inflation spike period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months, followed by a decline below 4.5%, predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as markets anticipate policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5 AND lag(UNRATE) <= 4.5 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4.5 in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the transition period.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (PAYEMS) exceed expectations by at least 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days is likely to be positive as it signals consumer spending resilience.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS actual > 105% of prior month forecast for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in consumer confidence (HOUST) creates a negative feedback loop that predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as weak supply meets strong demand, amplifying market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for the same month
failure_condition: During periods matching the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) without a corresponding decline in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days is expected to be positive as markets anticipate a structural supply-side recovery in the absence of inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or show high volatility without directional bias.
